 BADRUBEN MEHBUBBHAI IBRAHIMBHAI KHANUSIYA & ORS.

 Appearance:
 MR ASHISH M DAGLI(2203) for the Appellant(s) No. 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8  MR GC MAZMUDAR(1193) for the Defendant(s) No. 4  MR HG MAZMUDAR(1194) for the Defendant(s) No. 4  NOTICE ISSUED BY PUBLICATION for the Defendant(s) No. 1,2,3  ==========================================================
 CORAM:HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE J. C. DOSHI  Date : 11/10/2024  ORAL ORDER 1.

The present First Appeal, under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, is preferred by the appellants - original claimants, being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned common judgment and award dated 08.09.1996 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Aux.),
Sabarkantha at Himmatnagar in Motor Accident Claim Petition No.1424 of 1996, by which the Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.4,37,800/- from all opponents, jointly and severally.

2. Brief facts of the case are as under:
2.1 On 08.09.1996, deceased Mehbubbhai was driving the S.T.Bus No.GJ-18B-404 from Himmatnagar to Modasa with moderate speed on correct side of the Himmatnagar-Shamlaji N.H. No.8 near Agiyol -- Berna stand and at around 7.30 a.m., opponent No. 1 i.e. the driver of Luxury Bus No.GJ-12T-4166 came driving his bus from opposite direction with full speed NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2297/2009

ORDER DATED: 11/10/2024 undefined rashly and negligently on wrong side and dashed with the driver side of S.T. Bus No.GJ-18B-404 and thus the alleged accident occurred due to gross negligence on the part of luxury bus driver and due to the alleged accident,
deceased Mehbubbhai i.e. the S.T. driver sustained fatal injuries and succumbed to these Injuries and died on the spot.

The petitioner of M.AC.P. No.
1138/96 was serving as conductor in the involved S.T. bus and he has claimed Rs.2,00,000/- towards accidental injuries sustained by him in the alleged accident.
The petitioner of M.A.C.P. No. 1177/96 was traveling in the involved S.T. bus and he has claimed towards accidental injuries sustained by him in the alleged accident.

The G.S.R.T.e. has filed the clailn petition to recover compensation of Rs.1,00,000/-
towards damages caused to the involved S.T. Bus No.GJ-18B-404.
2.2

Therefore, the legal heirs of the deceased have filed claim petition seeking compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with cost and interest for unnatural and untimely death against the present respondents before the Tribunal.
2.3 The Tribunal has framed the issues.
The oral as well as documentary evidence were led by the rival parties before the Tribunal.
After considering the documentary as well as oral evidence and submissions made at the bar, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition by awarding compensation as noted above.
3. Learned advocate Mr.Ashish Dagli for the appellants - claimants has submitted that the Tribunal has committed an error in not properly calculating the amount of compensation.

He has NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2297/2009 ORDER DATED:
11/10/2024 undefined submitted that amount of award is on lower side as the Tribunal has not properly considered the various aspects; like prospective income of the deceased, negligence,
liability and family circumstances, etc.
He has submitted that the deceased was aged about only 46 years at the time of accident and was S.T. Bus driver.
He has submitted that at the relevant point of time, his monthly income was Rs.3,988/-.
He has submitted that the learned Tribunal has erred in considering the prospective income, deduction of personal expenses looking to the dependents and multiplier looking to the age of the deceased.

He has submitted that therefore, considering the loss of dependency, it would be calculated as Rs.3,988/- as monthly income plus Rs.1196/- as 30%
prospective income minus Rs.1036/- as personal expenses (1/5) multiplied by 12 months and multiplied by 13 multiplier would come to Rs.6,47,088/- total future loss, which should be awarded to the claimants by the learned Tribunal.
3.1 He has further submitted that considering the general and non-pecuniary damages, the learned Tribunal should award Rs.18,500/- each towards loss of estate and funeral expenses.

He has also submitted that towards loss of consortium, there are eight dependents and therefore, it would be awarded Rs.48,400/- to each dependent should be awarded as per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of United India Insurance Co. Ltd., versus Satinder Kaur @

To buttress his submission, he has relied upon the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in case of Chandra @ Chanda @ Chandraram and another Vs. Mukesh Kumar Badruben Mehbubbhai Ibrahimbhai ... vs Ramsingh Champakdan Thapa on 11 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27435913/

NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2297/2009 ORDER DATED: 11/10/2024 undefined 3.2
He has submitted that the compensation is required to be enhanced by modifying the award impugned accordingly and this appeal may be allowed.
4. Per contra, Mr.G.C.Mazmudar, learned advocate for respondent - Insurance Company has submitted that the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is just and proper.
The Tribunal has rightly considered the income of the deceased, the age of the deceased, the dependency and future aspect of income.
They have submitted that under the head of loss of estate and funeral expenses, the Tribunal has rightly awarded compensation.
They have submitted that the amount under the head of loss of consortium is just and proper.
They have submitted that this appeal may be dismissed and no interference be made by this Court.
5. It is noteworthy to mention that the provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 which gives paramount importance to the concept of 'just and fair' compensation.
It is a beneficial legislation which has been framed with the object of providing relief to the victims or their families.
Section 168 of the Motor Vehicles Act deals with the concept of 'just compensation' which ought to be determined on the foundation of fairness, reasonableness and equitability.

Although such determination can never be arithmetically exact or perfect, an endeavor should be made by the Court to award just and fair compensation irrespective of the amount claimed by the claimants.
6.1 I have considered the submissions made by the rival parties.
I have perused the record and proceedings of the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2297/2009 ORDER DATED: 11/10/2024 undefined Tribunal.
I have gone through the impugned judgment and award passed by the learned Tribunal.

From the record, it transpires that the deceased was aged about 46 years and was a S.T. driver and earning Rs.3,988/- as monthly income from S.T. Corporation and salary statement to that regard was also produced on record.
Therefore, it would meet the ends of justice if monthly income is considered Rs.3,988/-.
By adding 30% prospective income, it would come to Rs.5,184/- and therefore, total income comes to Rs.5,184/- per month.
Since at the time of accident, there were total eight dependents, 1/5 would be proper to be deducted as personal expenses and therefore, it would come to Rs.4,148/-.

Hence, the income would come to Rs.4,148/- per month and therefore,
yearly, it would come to Rs.49,776/-.

As the deceased is aged about 46 years, multiplier of 13 is proper as per the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma versus Delhi Transport Corporation reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, it would come to Rs.6,47,088/- as future loss,
which is required to be awarded to the claimants.
6.2

sentences.text: Further, considering the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Pranay Shethi (supra), as general and non-pecuniary damages, under the head of loss of estate and funeral expenses, if we award Rs.18,500/- each, which would be the just and proper compensation.
6.3 Further, there are eight dependents to the deceased.

Therefore, as per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of United India Insurance Co. Ltd., versus Satinder NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2297/2009 ORDER DATED: 11/10/2024 undefined Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur Badruben Mehbubbhai Ibrahimbhai ... vs Ramsingh Champakdan Thapa

 Particulars   Future Loss of Income   Loss of Estate   Funeral Expenses   Loss of consortium   Total...
Less : Amount which is already awarded   Additional amount which is awarded

7. Therefore, I hold that the claimants are entitled to get the total amount of compensation of Rs.10,42,488/- with 7.5% p.a. interest from the date of filing the claim petition till its realisation,
which would meet the ends of justice.
Rest of the direction(s) of the Tribunal remain same.
8. For the reasons recorded above, the following order is passed.
8.1 The present appeal is partly allowed.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2297/2009 ORDER DATED: 11/10/2024 undefined 8.2

The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the enhanced amount Rs.6,04,688/- with 7.5% p.a. interest from the date of claim petition till its realization before the concerned Tribunal, within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of this order.

8.3 The Tribunal shall disburse the entire awarded amount lying in the FDR and/or with the Tribunal, with accrued interest thereon, if any, to the claimants, by account payee cheque / NEFT /
RTGS, after proper verification and after following due procedure.
8.4 While making the payment, the Tribunal shall deduct the courts fees, if not paid, in accordance with rules/law.
8.5 Record and proceedings be sent back to the concerned Tribunal, forthwith.
